libraries.group: Effects, including the two the sandbox's ambient WASI makes real
JavaScript interop, which is what this arm's own SDK is built on

modules.brief: Find what the agent can call, and take a documentation view back out of the window.
modules.detail:
The system prompt names modules and no function at all, so this is the module every other one is reached through: `search` turns a keyword or a module id into fully-qualified names, and `Gg.Views.openDocsView` reads one of those names in full.

Searching is bound in every program whatever a run enables, because an agent must always be able to find the functions it does hold. Closing a documentation view is the exception and is bought by a capability: opening one only ever appends to the prompt, while closing one rewrites its middle, and those are different enough trades to be different decisions.

modules.brief: Read, write, edit and list the files of the workspace.
modules.detail:
Reading is the cheap direction of this sandbox and writing is the expensive one, so a program that reads a dozen files to decide what to change is well shaped, while one that rewrites forty large files in a single turn will exhaust its fuel budget.

Nothing here places anything in the agent's context window. `Gg.Views.openFile` is the call that does.

modules.brief: Run shell commands in the workspace.
modules.detail:
One function, and the way a program reaches everything gg has no tool for: a build, a test run, `git`, `curl`, a package manager. The workspace is the working directory.

A non-zero exit is a *result* rather than a failure, because deciding whether a build or a test run passed is the single most common thing a program does with one.

modules.brief: The epic and issue board: work decomposed into dispatchable units.
modules.detail:
An issue is the heavyweight unit of work — its scope, non-scope and completion criteria are exactly what a delegated child agent is briefed from — which is why creating one asks for more than adding a task does.

Two patch fields are **three-way**, and a record with optional fields says all three without a sentinel: leaving `description` out keeps it and `Nothing` clears it; leaving `epicId` out leaves the grouping alone and `Nothing` detaches the issue from its epic.

modules.brief: The task list, which is a directed acyclic graph rather than a list of lines.
modules.detail:
A task is the lightweight unit of work: an id, a title, and the tasks that must finish first. A unit heavy enough to brief a child agent from belongs on `Gg.Board` instead.

One spelling here is worth reading twice. A revision's `description` is a **three-way** edit, and a record with optional fields says all three without a sentinel: leaving the field out keeps the description, `Nothing` clears it, `Just` replaces it.

modules.brief: Durable notes that survive context compaction.
modules.detail:
A run picks one of three memory strategies and binds only that strategy's functions, so what this module offers is the honest answer to what memory can do here. The scratchpad keeps every memory in the context window (`writeMemory` and `updateMemory`); the two file-shaped strategies keep the contents outside it (`createMemory`, `readMemory` and `editMemory`), one behind an index that is always in context and one behind `searchMemories`. Deleting is bound under all three.

Every mutation hands back the budget after it, so a program decides whether to write another memory by reading numbers rather than by parsing a sentence about them.

modules.brief: The only way material enters the agent's own context window.
modules.detail: Under responses as code a whole program's output would otherwise collapse into one anonymous blob of logs, charged to one band, attributable to nothing and closable by nothing. A view restores what tool calling gave for free: one message per view, carrying the band it is charged to and the selector it can be closed by.

modules.brief: Managing the agent's own context window.
modules.detail: These are the only calls whose effect is on the conversation rather than on the workspace. They are worth making from a program precisely because a program can decide *when* to: read a set of files, extract what matters, then evict the views in the same turn.

modules.brief: Handing scoped work to child agents, and handing this session to another agent.
modules.detail:
Waiting can dominate a turn's wall clock — it blocks while real agents run — and the run's budget keeps ticking while it does. A program is therefore best shaped to spawn broadly and wait once, rather than to spawn and wait in a loop.

The brief is where this arm's types earn their keep: a child is briefed either with a self-contained `Prompt` or with a board `Issue`, and because that choice is a sum type rather than two optional fields, "both" and "neither" are programs that do not compile.

A skill name is a plain `String` rather than the arm of a sum type, because the catalogue is per run while this SDK is compiled once. The names available are listed in the system prompt, and an unknown one comes back as `NotFound` carrying the full list.

modules.brief: The library of programs this agent has already run.
modules.detail:
Under responses as code a reply is a whole program, so a one-character mistake in a sixty-line program costs the sixty lines again. The library makes the fix proportional to the mistake: fetch what ran, patch it with ordinary string work, hand it back.

```
source <- Gg.Programs.get {}
Gg.Programs.rerun (replaceAll (Pattern "readfile") (Replacement "readFile") source)
```

modules.brief: Ending the session, one group of calls per role.
modules.detail:
Under responses as code every reply is a program, so there is no prose turn that could mean "the work is done" — a model that answers "task complete" has written a reply that failed to be a program, not an ending. These are the calls that mean it.

Exactly one group is bound. An agent whose role is to do work gets `finish`; a reviewer gets `approve` and `requestChanges` instead, because a reviewer's result has a shape of its own: not what was done, but whether it may stand.

None of them stops the program. Whatever follows still runs, so an ending belongs last, once the calls before it have confirmed the work. A program that then fails revokes the ending and earns another turn.

modules.brief: The types every other module's signatures name, and the three functions that read a failure.
modules.detail:
A capability module owns the types it produces, so `Gg.Files.FileRead` belongs to `Gg.Files` and `Gg.Board.IssueCreated` to `Gg.Board`. The two here belong to none of them because they belong to all: every call in this SDK throws a `ToolError`, and every one of them is classified by a `ToolErrorCode`.

```
import Gg.Core as Gg.Core
import Gg.Files as Gg.Files

outcome <- Gg.Core.attempt (Gg.Files.readTextFile "notes.md" {})
```

A failing call **throws** rather than handing back an `Either`. That is how effectful PureScript expresses a failure that is usually fatal to the work in hand, and it keeps the happy path unwrapped: `read <- Gg.Files.readTextFile "main.purs" {}` binds a `String`. An expected failure is narrowed with `attempt`, which converts one gg failure into an `Either` and re-throws anything that is not gg's.

functions.name: search
functions.brief: Search every function and type the agent can call, by keyword and by filter.
functions.detail:
This is how a name is found. Matching is a case-insensitive substring over names, signatures, briefs and detailed descriptions, so `docs` finds `openDocsView`. Ranking is by the kind of evidence that matched — an entry whose own name matched outranks one that merely mentions the word in a paragraph — and a weaker kind never overtakes a stronger one however often it occurs.

Only entries this run bound are returned, so nothing a search finds is something the run withheld. The filters compose with each other and with the query.

The page comes back as a value and is also opened as a view, under the selector `search results`, so it can be read on the next turn without a program showing it to itself. The next search replaces that view: it names what is being worked from rather than keeping a record.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` for an empty query with no filter at all — nothing matched and nothing was asked for are different answers — and for a `limit` of zero, which asks for a page that answers nothing. A module or type name gg does not hold is not among them: it matches nothing.

signatures.signature: search :: String -> { module? :: String, type? :: String, kind? :: Gg.Docs.DocKind, offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int } -> Effect Gg.Docs.DocSearch

parameters.name: query
parameters.doc: The words to match, as a case-insensitive substring. It may be empty when at least one filter is given.

parameters.name: options
parameters.type: { module? :: String, type? :: String, kind? :: Gg.Docs.DocKind, offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int }
parameters.doc: The filters and the page; `{}` ranks the query alone.

fields.name: module
fields.doc: One module's id — `files`, `views`, `docs` — matched exactly. An empty query with a module is that module's whole directory rather than a search. A module filter is a lookup, so a name no module has matches nothing rather than failing.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: One type's name, narrowing to that type and to the functions that take or return it. Like `options.module`, a name nothing declares matches nothing rather than failing.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Whether to return functions or types. The default returns both.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: How many hits to skip, for reading past the first page. The default starts at the best hit.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: The most hits to return. The default is gg's own page size and there is a ceiling above it, so comparing the hits against `total` is the only way to see a capped page. Zero is refused rather than read as "no cap".

functions.name: close
functions.brief: Take one documentation view out of the context window, by the key it was opened under.
functions.detail:
How many were closed comes back; a key that is not open closes `0` rather than failing. The removal has no cascade: closing a type's view leaves every function view beside it, and closing a function's leaves its types. Nothing records why a view was opened, so a type that is closed is opened again by the next function that mentions it.

# Raises

`Unavailable` under a run that did not enable closing documentation views.

parameters.name: key
parameters.doc: The fully-qualified name the view was opened under, as a search hit reports it.

functions.name: closeAll
functions.brief: Take every documentation view out of the context window and report how many went.
functions.detail:
The blanket form of `close`, on exactly the same terms and behind the same capability: no cascade to consider because nothing is left, and `0` rather than a failure when none was open.

# Raises

`Unavailable` under a run that did not enable closing documentation views.

functions.name: readFile
functions.brief: Read a file, as either the `TextFile` or the `ImageFile` arm of a `Gg.Files.FileRead`.
functions.detail:
Which of the two comes back is detected from the file's bytes, never from the extension, so a mislabelled picture is still a picture. The sum is closed, so an ordinary `case` needs no catch-all:

```
read <- Gg.Files.readFile "logo.png" {}
case read of
  Gg.Files.TextFile text -> Gg.Views.openText "logo" text.contents
  Gg.Files.ImageFile picture -> Gg.Views.openText "logo" picture.label
```

A relative path resolves against the workspace; an absolute one is read as given, so anything else in this container — an offloaded command's output under `/tmp/gg-shell`, say — is readable. This call hands bytes to the program and places nothing in the context window, and reading a picture describes it without showing it, so a file only read here is a file nobody has looked at.

# Raises

`NotFound` for a missing path.

parameters.doc: The file to read, relative to the workspace or absolute.

parameters.name: options

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: The 1-based line to start at. Honoured only under a capped read policy.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: How many lines to return from `offset`. Honoured only under a capped read policy.

functions.brief: Read a text file and hand back its contents directly.

`Gg.Files.readFile` without the narrowing, for the common case: the same read, the same window, the same cost.

`InvalidArgument` when the path names a picture, which `Gg.Files.readFile` inspects instead and `Gg.Views.openFile` displays.

functions.detail:
Widening the surrounding context until the match is unique is the way to disambiguate; counting occurrences is not.

`NotFound` when the text does not appear, and `Conflict` — with the number of matches — when it appears more than once.

functions.brief: List a directory, sorted by name; `{}` lists the workspace root.
functions.detail: Each entry carries a bare `name` — join it with the directory that was listed — and its `kind`. An empty directory is an empty array, not a failure.

functions.name: shell
functions.brief: Run a command with `sh -c` in the workspace directory and collect its merged output.
functions.detail:
A non-zero exit is not a failure: it arrives as `exitCode` on the result, and only a process that could not be launched, or one the timeout killed, raises.

This run may **offload** shell output, and the `shell` tool's own description says which mode is in force. Under `offload`, `output` holds only the tail that fits and ends with a note naming the two files the command's full stdout and stderr were written to. Under `adaptive`, the default, a command that succeeded returns no output at all beyond that note, and one that failed returns the tail. Grepping the named files beats re-running the command.

# Raises

`LimitExceeded` when the timeout killed the process, and `IoError` when it could not be launched.

signatures.signature: shell :: String -> { timeoutSecs? :: Int } -> Effect Gg.Shell.ShellOutput

parameters.name: command
parameters.doc: The command line, run by `sh -c` with the workspace as its working directory.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: How to run it; `{}` takes gg's own defaults.

fields.name: timeoutSecs
fields.doc: How long to let it run, in seconds, before killing it. Left out, gg's default of 120 applies, clamped to whatever is left of the run's wall-clock budget.

functions.name: createEpic
functions.brief: Create an epic to group related issues.
functions.detail:
The id the prefix resolved to comes back with the board budget. A prefix is 3-6 letters naming the epic; it is upper-cased and becomes the epic's id, which is also what its issues are numbered from — a prefix of `auth` gives issues `AUTH-1`, `AUTH-2`, and so on.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` when the prefix is not 3-6 letters, and `Conflict` when another epic already holds it.

functions.name: createIssue
functions.brief: Create a self-contained, dispatchable issue.
functions.detail:
The id the board **assigned** comes back with the board budget: it is numbered under its epic's prefix (`AUTH-1`, `AUTH-2`, …), or under `ISSUE` when it has no epic, and the caller does not choose it — so keeping the returned id is what blocks a later issue on this one or waits for it. `inScope`, `outOfScope` and `completionCriteria` are what a child agent is briefed from, so they are written for a reader with no other context.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` when `agent` or a reviewer is not one this agent may assign, and `Conflict` on a blocker edge that would close a cycle.

functions.name: waitForIssue
functions.brief: Register a wait on an issue and hand back an acknowledgement.
functions.detail:
Nothing blocks inside the program: the wait is recorded and the call returns at once, so the rest of the program still runs. Once it ends the run suspends, freeing this agent's slot for others, until the issue is terminal — done, or failed if its assigned agent could not complete it — and then resumes on the next turn. It is how the next turn's work is sequenced behind an issue this one depends on. The issue this agent was assigned to implement is not one it may wait on.

# Raises

`NotFound` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue to wait on. It may not be the issue this agent was assigned.

functions.name: writeMemory
functions.brief: Record a durable memory that survives context compaction.
functions.detail:
A memory may also carry **code**. `code` is a PureScript module whose exports are bound at `lib.<name>` in every later program, so a helper got right once is never written again; `onUse` is a script gg runs the first time the memory comes into use, whose views arrive on the next turn. Neither is context — they cost no window, are never shown back, and count against no body limit — and both are bounded on their own.

# Raises

`Conflict` on a duplicate name, and `LimitExceeded` when the body would breach the run's caps — revising or deleting a memory beats accruing more.

fields.doc: A PureScript module whose exports are bound at `lib.<name>` for the rest of the session. Left out for a memory that is only prose.

It takes a slug, a one-line description — required where the run keeps an index, since that is the memory's line in it — and the initial contents. It may also carry `code`, a module bound at `lib.<name>` once the memory is read, and `onUse`, a script run on that first read.

`Conflict` on a duplicate slug, and `LimitExceeded` when the contents, or the index entry, would breach a limit.

A memory that carries code loads that code as it is read: the reply names the `lib.<key>` it is bound at, and it stays bound for the rest of the session.

# Raises

`NotFound` when no memory has that slug.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory's slug.

functions.name: editMemory
functions.brief: Revise a memory in place, replacing the one exact occurrence of `search` with `replace`.
functions.detail:
Appending is quoting the last line and replacing it with itself plus what is being added.

# Raises

`NotFound` when the text does not appear, `Conflict` when it appears more than once, `LimitExceeded` when the result would be too long, and `InvalidArgument` when the edit would leave the memory empty — deleting it is the call for that.

signatures.signature: editMemory :: { name :: String, search :: String, replace :: String } -> Effect Gg.Memories.MemoryUsage

parameters.name: edit
parameters.type: { name :: String, search :: String, replace :: String }
parameters.doc: The revision to make.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The slug of the memory to revise.

fields.name: search
fields.doc: The exact text to find in its contents. It must appear exactly once.

fields.name: replace
fields.doc: The text to put in its place.

functions.name: searchMemories
functions.brief: Find the memories mentioning any of the given keywords, best first.
functions.detail:
Plain case-insensitive substring matching over each memory's slug, description and contents, ranked by how many of the keywords a memory mentions and then by how often. Several specific words rank better than one sentence, and the hits worth having in full are then read. A search that matches nothing is an empty array.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` when every keyword is empty.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.doc: The words to look for. Several specific words rank better than one sentence, because a memory is ranked by how many of them it mentions.

functions.name: deleteMemory
functions.brief: Evict a memory by name, freeing room in the budget.
functions.detail:
# Raises

`NotFound` when no memory has that name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory's slug.

functions.name: openFile
functions.brief: Read a file and place it in the context window, keyed by its path.
functions.detail:
The value handed back is exactly what `Gg.Files.readFile` returns, and the file also becomes its own context item, attributed to its path and closable by it. The split from `Gg.Files.readFile` is the point: that call gets bytes for the program, this one puts a file in front of the model, so a program that reads forty files to grep them still costs no window.

`offset` and `limit` select a window of lines, and two pages of one file are two views that coexist; re-opening the same page replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate. An image file is displayed as a picture, and this is the only call that displays one — reading an image describes it without showing it.

signatures.signature: openFile :: String -> { offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int } -> Effect Gg.Files.FileRead

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to open, relative to the workspace or absolute.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: The window of lines to show; `{}` shows the whole file.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: The 1-based line to start at.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: How many lines to show from `offset`.

functions.name: openText
functions.brief: Place a value the program computed in the context window, under a label.
functions.detail:
A directory listing, a command's output, a child agent's answer, an assembled table: this is the channel into the window, and a value a program computes reaches the model on no other. Opening the same label again replaces what it showed, so a program may refine a view in a loop without piling up a copy per iteration. An empty body is allowed, since it is how a program says that something it was showing is now empty.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` for an empty label — a view with no selector could never be closed or attributed — and `LimitExceeded`, naming the cap, for a body or label over gg's caps; nothing is ever silently truncated.

parameters.name: label
parameters.doc: What to file the view under. It is what closes the view, and opening the same label again replaces what it showed. It may not be empty.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: What to show. An empty body is allowed: it is how a program says that something it was showing is now empty.

functions.name: openDocsView
functions.brief: Place one function's full documentation in the context window.
functions.detail:
Its signature, its description, and the declarations of any types it refers to that have not already been shown this session. This is a **view** rather than a return value: the documentation arrives in the next prompt under a `Documentation` heading keyed by the function name, exactly as a file or a computed value arrives, so it is not available in the turn that asks for it. Asking in one turn and using it in the next is the shape that works. Opening the same function's documentation again replaces the view rather than adding a second copy.

# Raises

`NotFound` for an unknown or unbound name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The function to document, by its fully-qualified name — `"Gg.Files.readFile"`. Searching the documentation is what names the functions that exist.

functions.name: close
functions.brief: Close every view carrying a selector, freeing the tokens they occupied.
functions.detail:
How many were closed comes back. For a file that is every page of that path, for a text view the one with that label, for the results of a search the label `search results`. Closing a selector that is not open hands back `0` rather than failing, so a program that tidies up unconditionally needs no guard on every call. Closing a file view forgets what was read rather than what exists; closing a text view discards the only copy of what it held, so anything needed later belongs in a file or a memory first.

Documentation views are not reached from here. `Gg.Docs.close` is what takes one away, and it is bought by a capability this call is not — so a sweep that included them would hand back `0` for an agent that may not close one, which reads as a selector that named nothing.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.doc: What the view is filed under: a file's path, a text view's label, or `search results`.

functions.name: current
functions.brief: List what is open in the context window right now.
functions.detail: Each view's `kind`, the `selector` that closes it, roughly what it costs in `tokens`, and — for a paged file view — the `region` it covers. What it enumerates is the context window's contents, not any module's functions. Reading it is what informs a decision about what to close when the window is filling up.

functions.name: evictFileView
functions.brief: Drop the contents of files already read out of the context window, freeing the tokens they occupy.
functions.detail: What that reclaimed comes back. The files on disk are untouched: this forgets what was read, not what exists.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: Which file's views to drop; `{}` drops every file view held.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: The file whose views to drop.

functions.name: archiveThread
functions.brief: Move whole turns out of the context window and report what that reclaimed.
functions.detail:
Every result carries a header with its turn number and roughly what holding it costs, so the turns worth dropping can be named: a span is inclusive at both ends, so `[ { from: 4, to: 19 } ]` archives turns 4 through 19. The agent's own messages in an archived turn are dropped; the results are kept and stay searchable.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` for a span whose ends are not turn numbers.

parameters.name: ranges
parameters.doc: The inclusive spans of turn numbers to move out of the window.

functions.name: searchArchive
functions.brief: Search archived history for a case-insensitive substring, most recent first, up to 8 hits.
functions.detail: `archiveEmpty` is worth checking before `hits`: it distinguishes nothing having been archived yet from a search that ran and matched nothing, so a second archive is not made in the belief that the first one failed.

parameters.name: query
parameters.doc: The substring to look for. Matching is case-insensitive.

functions.name: compact
functions.brief: Compact the context window: the detailed thread is dropped and restarted from a summary.
functions.detail:
Each path in `files` is read afresh into the restarted window. Skills, memories and the task list are kept as they are. gg asks for this call when the window is full, and refuses every other call until it is made.

It does not stop the program: it registers the request and returns, and the rewrite happens once the program has ended. Everything not in the summary and not in `files` is gone, so the summary is written for the agent that resumes, and the files it will need in hand are named.

# Raises

`Refused` when a compaction is already in flight and this call is not the one it asked for.

signatures.signature: compact :: String -> { files? :: Array String } -> Effect Unit

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: What the restarted window opens with. Everything not in it and not re-read from `files` is gone.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: What to read back into the restarted window; `{}` reads nothing back.

fields.name: files
fields.doc: The paths to read afresh into the restarted window. Defaults to none.

functions.name: spawnSubagent
functions.brief: Delegate scoped work to a child agent, which runs in parallel while this program continues.
functions.detail:
Its handle comes back immediately. The `agent` names the profile to run it as — one of the agents this one may spawn, which the system prompt lists — and it selects the child's model, tools and instructions. The brief is either `Gg.Delegation.Prompt "self-contained instructions"` or `Gg.Delegation.Issue "AUTH-1"`. The child shares this agent's workspace.

# Raises

`LimitExceeded` at the delegation depth cap, and `InvalidArgument` when `agent` is not one this agent may spawn.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent profile to run the child as, from the ones this agent may spawn. It selects the child's model, tools and instructions.

parameters.name: brief
parameters.doc: What the child is to do: `Gg.Delegation.Prompt` with self-contained instructions, or `Gg.Delegation.Issue` with the id of a board issue to brief it from.

functions.name: waitForSubagents
functions.brief: Block until the named children have finished, and collect their results in dispatch order.
functions.detail:
With `{}` it waits for every outstanding child. The run's wall-clock budget keeps running while it waits, so one wait for many children costs far less than one wait per child.

# Raises

`NotFound` for an unknown id.

signatures.signature: waitForSubagents :: { ids? :: Array String } -> Effect (Array Gg.Delegation.SubagentResult)

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: Which children to wait for; `{}` waits for every one still outstanding.

fields.name: ids
fields.doc: The children to wait for, as their handles named them.

functions.name: sendMessage
functions.brief: Deliver a message to a running child agent's inbox, which it reads at its next turn.
functions.detail:
# Raises

`NotFound` for an unknown agent id, and `Conflict` when that child has already returned.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.doc: The child to deliver to, as its handle named it.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to put in its inbox.

functions.name: transitionState
functions.brief: Move the process this session runs inside on to another of its states.
functions.detail:
The state is named the way an agent to spawn is named. It is bound only when a state machine is driving the session and the current state has somewhere to go. Like a compaction it is registered rather than performed: the call validates the target, returns, and the program runs on to its end — the transition happens after that, because replacing the agent and its window mid-program would pull every remaining call out from under it. The first declaration in a turn is the one that stands.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` for a state this session may not move to, and `Refused` for a second declaration in one turn.

signatures.signature: transitionState :: String -> { note? :: String } -> Effect Unit

parameters.name: state
parameters.doc: The state to move on to, named the way an agent to spawn is named.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: What to tell the next state's agent; `{}` tells it nothing.

fields.name: note
fields.doc: The opening message the next state's agent sees.

functions.name: exec
functions.brief: Continue this session as a different agent, from the next turn.
functions.detail:
The named agent takes over with its own model, tools and instructions, keeping every capability the two of them share — and the whole conversation above all, so it needs no catching up. Registered rather than performed, exactly as a state transition is and for the same reason: the window would otherwise be pulled out from under the program still composing into it. A session makes one succession per turn. It is bound only when this agent may make agent transitions and has agents it may become, and never while a state machine is driving the session.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` for an agent this agent may not become, and `Refused` for a second succession in one turn.

signatures.signature: exec :: String -> { prompt? :: String } -> Effect Unit

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to become, from the ones this agent may become.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: What to tell it; `{}` tells it nothing.

fields.name: prompt
fields.doc: Its opening message. It already has the whole conversation, so this is the instruction rather than a briefing.

functions.name: fork
functions.brief: Run a copy of this agent, in parallel, on something it will not do itself.
functions.detail:
The copy has the same model, the same tools and a private copy of the whole conversation, so the prompt is the *difference* rather than a briefing — everything already worked out is there.

Its handle comes back immediately, and the copy itself starts once this turn's results are recorded, because the conversation it inherits has to be a complete one. A wait can therefore collect it only on a later turn, never in the program that made it.

# Raises

`LimitExceeded` at the delegation depth cap.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: What the copy is to do instead. It has the whole conversation already, so this is the difference rather than a briefing.

functions.name: readSkill
functions.brief: Read a skill by name, handing back its body with the front matter stripped.
functions.detail:
Reading it also pins that body permanently into the context window, so a skill once read stays read. A skill may be **code** rather than prose, or as well as it: code is bound at `lib.<key>` for the rest of the session and the reply names the key and what it exports, reachable through `Gg.Core.lib`. An on-use script runs once the program has ended, and whatever it shows arrives on the next turn.

# Raises

`NotFound`, listing the skills that do exist, when the name is unknown.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The skill's name, as the system prompt lists it.

functions.name: history
functions.brief: The programs already run this session, oldest first.
functions.detail: Each carries the turn it ran on, how big it was, and whether it ran to its end. It lists shapes rather than sources, so the one worth having is then fetched. The list survives a compaction, which makes it the way to find a program whose text has left the context window. A session that has run nothing yet gets an empty array rather than an error.

functions.name: get
functions.brief: The exact source of one program that ran, as a string. With `{}`, the most recent one.
functions.detail:
This is the first half of fixing a program without rewriting it: get what ran, patch it with ordinary string work, and hand the result back to be run. What comes back is the program that **executed**, so when a turn's program was itself handed over, the answer is the program that ran rather than the few lines that asked for it — and fetch, patch and run compose turn after turn.

# Raises

`NotFound`, naming the turns that are held, for a turn that ran no program or one old enough that the library has dropped it.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: Which program to fetch; `{}` fetches the most recent one.

fields.name: turn
fields.doc: The turn whose program to fetch, as the history reports it.

functions.name: rerun
functions.brief: Hand gg a program to run in place of this one.
functions.detail:
This program finishes, then gg compiles and runs the given source as this turn's program. Paired with a fetch it fixes a program without re-emitting it. Nothing is undone: every call this program already made stands, and the program that runs next sees the world this one left behind, so handing over comes before work that should not be done twice.

The first call stands, because a silently replaced program is a change nobody can see. A program that then fails cancels the hand-over along with everything else it decided, and the turn ends as an ordinary error. Chains are bounded: one hand-over per turn, and the fixed program does the work.

# Raises

`Refused` for a second hand-over in one turn, and `InvalidArgument` for a blank source.

parameters.name: source
parameters.doc: The program to run in place of this one, as PureScript. It may not be blank.

functions.name: finish
functions.brief: End the session, reporting what was done in a sentence or two.
functions.detail: This is the only thing that ends it. It does not stop the program — whatever follows still runs — so it belongs last, once the calls before it have confirmed the work is really done. A program that then fails cancels the ending and earns another turn.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: What was done, in a sentence or two.

functions.name: approve
functions.brief: Accept the work under review: it meets every completion criterion and stays in scope.
functions.detail: This ends the session, and does not stop the program, so it belongs last — once the change has actually been read.

functions.name: requestChanges
functions.brief: Reject the work under review, listing every change that must be made before it can be accepted.
functions.detail:
Each item says what is wrong and what to change. The list may not be empty. This ends the session, and does not stop the program.

# Raises

`InvalidArgument` when the list is empty.

parameters.name: items
parameters.doc: Every change that must be made before the work can be accepted, one per entry: what is wrong, and what to change. It may not be empty.

members.brief: Approximately how many tokens that freed.

members.name: paths
members.brief: The workspace paths whose views were evicted. Empty for an archive.

members.name: detail
members.brief: The prose summary of what was reclaimed.

types.name: TurnRange
types.declaration: type TurnRange = { from :: Int, to :: Int }
types.brief: An inclusive span of turn numbers, the unit an archive moves out of the window.
types.detail: The numbers are the ones on the header of every result the agent is given, so `{ from: 4, to: 19 }` means exactly the turns numbered 4 through 19, both ends included.

members.name: from
members.brief: The first turn in the span.

members.name: to
members.brief: The last turn in the span, inclusive.

types.name: ArchiveHit
types.declaration: type ArchiveHit = { seq :: Int, role :: Gg.Context.MessageRole, text :: String }
types.brief: One archived message that matched a search.

members.name: seq
members.brief: The archived message's sequence number.

members.name: role
members.brief: Who said it.

members.name: text
members.brief: The message text.

types.name: MessageRole
types.declaration: data MessageRole = SystemMessage | UserMessage | AssistantMessage | ToolMessage
types.brief: Who said an archived message.

members.name: SystemMessage
members.brief: The system prompt.

members.name: UserMessage
members.brief: A turn's input: a result, a view, or an operator's instruction.

members.name: AssistantMessage
members.brief: Something the agent itself said.

members.name: ToolMessage
members.brief: A tool result, on a session that made tool calls rather than writing programs.

types.name: ArchiveSearch
types.declaration: type ArchiveSearch = { archiveEmpty :: Boolean, hits :: Array Gg.Context.ArchiveHit }
types.brief: What a search of the archive found.

members.name: archiveEmpty
members.brief: Nothing has been archived yet, so there was nothing to search.
members.detail: Deliberately distinct from a search that ran and matched nothing, so that a second archive is not made in the belief that the first one failed.

members.name: hits
members.brief: The matches, most recent first, at most 8.

types.name: Brief
types.declaration: data Brief = Prompt String | Issue String
types.brief: What a child agent is briefed with.
types.detail: The choice is a type rather than a pair of optional fields, so "both" and "neither" are programs that do not compile instead of calls that fail at run time.

members.name: Prompt
members.brief: Self-contained instructions for a child that needs no other context.

members.name: Issue
members.brief: The id of a board issue to brief the child from.

types.name: SubagentHandle
types.declaration: type SubagentHandle = { id :: String, slot :: String, modelId :: String }
types.brief: A child agent that was spawned and is now running in parallel.

members.name: id
members.brief: The child's id, which is what waits for it or sends it a message.

members.name: slot
members.brief: The agent profile it runs as.

members.name: modelId
members.brief: The model actually bound to that agent.

types.name: AgentEnding
types.declaration: data AgentEnding = AgentCompleted | AgentExhausted | AgentTimedOut | AgentModelError | AgentAuthError | AgentLimitExceeded
types.brief: How a child agent's loop ended — gg's own six words, as the tool-calling path also reports them.

members.name: AgentCompleted
members.brief: It finished normally, and its summary is what it returned.

members.name: AgentExhausted
members.brief: It reached the per-run turn ceiling.

members.name: AgentTimedOut
members.brief: It passed its wall-clock deadline.

members.name: AgentModelError
members.brief: A model turn failed.

members.name: AgentAuthError
members.brief: The run's credential was refused.

members.name: AgentLimitExceeded
members.brief: An execution ceiling stopped it: consecutive errors, error rate, or cost.

types.name: SubagentResult
types.declaration: type SubagentResult = { id :: String, status :: Maybe Gg.Delegation.AgentEnding, summary :: String }
types.brief: One child agent's collected result.

members.name: id
members.brief: The child's id.

members.name: status
members.brief: How it finished; `Nothing` when it produced no return value at all.

members.name: summary
members.brief: Its final message.

types.name: ProgramSummary
types.declaration: type ProgramSummary = { turn :: Int, lines :: Int, chars :: Int, ok :: Boolean, error :: Maybe String }
types.brief: One program that has already run, as the library's directory lists it.
types.detail: It describes the program's **shape**, never its source: a directory that inlined every program would put the whole session back in the context window, which is the one thing the library exists to avoid.

members.name: turn
members.brief: The turn it ran on, which is what fetches its source.

members.name: lines
members.brief: How many lines of source it was.

members.name: chars
members.brief: How many characters of source it was.

members.name: ok
members.brief: Whether it ran to its end, with no uncaught failure and no sandbox ceiling stopping it.

members.name: error
members.brief: The error it ended with, when it did not run to its end.

types.name: ToolError
types.declaration: type ToolError = { tool :: String, code :: Gg.Core.ToolErrorCode, message :: String }
types.brief: A gg call that failed, thrown by every function in this SDK.
types.detail: An expected failure is caught with `attempt` and branched on its `code`; an unexpected one is left to escape, and gg reports which call failed and where the program had reached.

members.name: tool
members.brief: The gg call that failed, under gg's own name for it.
members.detail: `read_file`, `spawn_subagent`: the vocabulary a run's enabled set is expressed in rather than this SDK's spelling of it.

members.name: code
members.brief: The failure class, so a catch site branches on a value rather than on prose.

members.name: message
members.brief: What went wrong, in gg's words. Worth showing in a view; not worth matching on.

types.name: ToolErrorCode
types.declaration: data ToolErrorCode = InvalidArgument | NotFound | Conflict | Refused | Unavailable | LimitExceeded | IoError | OtherFailure
types.brief: Why a gg call failed — the `code` a catch site branches on instead of matching on prose.

members.name: InvalidArgument
members.brief: The arguments were malformed, ill-typed, or out of range.
members.detail: It covers a path that is absolute or climbs out of the workspace, and an agent name this run does not declare.

members.name: NotFound
members.brief: The named thing does not exist.
members.detail: A file, a skill, a memory, a task, an epic, an issue, a subagent, a stored program, or a documentation entry.

members.name: Conflict
members.brief: Well-formed, and in conflict with the current state.
members.detail: An ambiguous edit, a dependency cycle, a duplicate id, a subagent that has already returned.

members.name: Refused
members.brief: gg refused the call on a rule about the session's state.
members.detail: A compaction in flight that this call is not the one it asked for, a memory call while memories are read-only, a second ending or hand-over in a turn that already declared one, or a hook that blocked it. A ceiling that was reached is `LimitExceeded` rather than this.

members.name: Unavailable
members.brief: The call exists and this run's capability set does not offer it.
members.detail: Every name in this SDK is in scope whatever a run enables, because the library is compiled once and a run's capability set is decided per run — so a withheld call arrives as this rather than as a compile error.

members.name: LimitExceeded
members.brief: A gg-side ceiling was reached.
members.detail: A shell timeout, a store cap, the delegation depth cap, or the run's wall-clock budget.

members.name: IoError
members.brief: The underlying input, output or process failed.

members.name: OtherFailure
members.brief: The failure was not classified.
members.detail: Reserved for outcomes raised outside a tool implementation. The one this SDK can raise itself is a call it declares that the run's guest does not export — a mismatch between the two artifacts rather than anything a program did, and never a capability that was withheld, which is `Unavailable` and comes from the host.
